newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds swept up by U.S. treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds swept up by U.S. treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds rallied in early trading Friday in keeping with U.S. treasuries, which surged on much weaker-than-expected jobs data, dealers said.
"The market shot up at the opening and then curbed gains a bit, but it's likely to stay well in positive territory throughout the session," said one dealer at a large local brokerage.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 jumped to 119.10 from 118.8 at the close Thursday, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/2 to 85.

"The news from New York is going to dominate the session today. I don't think anyone will care about anything else now ahead of the weekend, although of course eventually we may see some profit-taking," said another trader.

The U.S. Labor Department reported September non-farm payrolls fell 40,000 against an expected rise of 166,000. Analysts noted, however, that average hourly earnings rose 0.5 percent against a forecast of 0.2 percent and the average work week was also slightly longer than expected.
